English: Tether Post
A crude line of wooden posts and rope, used for securing horses and pack animals near the castle walls. Provides only the most basic shelter and security for mounts.
Wooden Stable
Simple wooden sheds built to shelter horses and provide basic fodder storage, improving the readiness of light cavalry and messengers.
Stone Stable
Robust stables of stone and timber, with secure stalls and better feed. Allows for more horses and improved cavalry musters.
Covered Stable
Enclosed, well-ventilated stables with sloped roofs, haylofts, and drainage, providing superior care and rapid readiness for horses.
Horse Corral
A broad, fenced corral for breaking, training and exercising horses, improving cavalry readiness and the quality of mounts.
Equerry
A dedicated equerry oversees horse breeding, training, and logistics, ensuring elite mounts for knights and officers.
Large Stable
Expansive stables, with multiple wings and improved hay storage, able to support a sizeable remount herd and a permanent stablemaster.
Stud Farm
A sprawling stud farm breeds and raises warhorses, greatly increasing both the quantity and quality of cavalry the castle can maintain.
Armored Stall
Specialized stalls for the housing and care of destriers and armored chargers, allowing for the creation and support of heavily-armored cavalry.
Noble Stables
Opulent, fortified stables reserved for the steeds of noblemen and knights. A symbol of prestige and martial power, granting unmatched cavalry muster and status.
